PC: Generally, pruritis can be managed with oral diphenhydramine and acetaminophen.
Hydroxyzine or topical creams can also be useful.
With more severe cases, corticosteroids can be used as well.
If you see red flag signs, such as facial swelling, hypotension, or shock, intramuscular epinephrine should be used for anaphylactic reaction.
SBP: If you are concerned for anaphylaxis, you should make the ICU and/or anesthesia aware of the patient, as they may need to be intubated for airway protection.
